newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey opposition sees record C/A deficit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Turkey opposition sees record C/A deficit in 1996.

text.p: Turkey's main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz said the current account deficit may hit a record high of $8 billion this year.

"It is predicted that the foreign trade deficit may stand at $22 to $23 billion and the current account deficit at $7-8 billion at the end of this year," Yilmaz told a group meeting of his centre-right Motherland Party.
The government's official target for this year is $16 billion. But economists expect the 1996 current account deficit to exceed this target in line with a deterioration in the trade balance.
The trade deficit was $2.4 billion in the first two months of 1996 after $14.1 bilion for the whole 1995. The official target for this year is $16 billion.

The current account gave a surplus of $277 million in January after a deficit of $2.3 billion in 1995. The country faced its highest current account gap in 1993 when it showed a deficit of $6.4 billion.

Technical problems caused by a January customs pact with the European Union have delayed announcement of official trade and current account figures. Officials say February balance of payments figures may be unveiled on Thursday.
